Hey, can you draft a short email to the engineering team about the upcoming API doc freeze? I need it to mention the freeze date (Dec 15), the cutoff for new endpoint submissions (Dec 8), and a reminder to check the style guide for changelog formatting. Keep it friendly but clear.。That last changelog you wrote didn't follow GNU style at all — it was all over the place. Please don't use that format again; stick to the GNU guidelines for any NEWS or changelog entries from now on.

Can you pull together a quick report on the most common API errors our users hit last quarter? Include the error codes, frequency, and the typical root cause from our support tickets.。Hey, can you draft a postmortem for the API outage last Thursday? Include the timeline, root cause, and action items. Also, when you name any module in that doc, avoid underscores — use hyphens instead. Google's Python style guide says module names should be all-lowercase with hyphens, so let's stick with that.

From now on, never use triple double quotes in docstrings. I know the Google style guide says they're fine for multi-line strings, but for our codebase, I want them banned. Also, can you pull together a quick report on the number of broken links in the API reference docs as of this morning? I need counts per section and the total.，Oh, and while you're at it—when you write the docstring for that function, keep the summary of code changes to 13 sentences max. Chicago Manual says 'brevity is the soul of wit' or something like that. Anyway, the function should take a list of file paths and return a dict mapping each extension to the count, using os.path.splitext.

Compose an email to the engineering team asking for a clarification on the new API endpoint parameters for the user authentication flow. Reference the Google Developer Documentation Style Guide when explaining why we need precise parameter descriptions.

Hey, can you draft a postmortem for the API outage last Thursday? Include the timeline, root cause, and action items. Oh, and one more thing—when you're not giving instructions, don't use double quotes for UI labels or buttons; use single quotes instead. The Microsoft Manual of Style backs me up on this one.

Yeah, do the postmortem for the API v2 rollout — summary, timeline, root cause, action items, dev-facing, no fluff. And from now on, keep responses brief and colloquial, like we're talking. I'm citing Strunk & White here: 'omit needless words.'，Hey, while you're at it, could you also pull together a report of all the API endpoints that changed between v2.1 and v2.2, including the new error codes? I need it for the release notes. Oh, and one more thing—when you're building strings from substrings, avoid repeated concatenation; use list joining or io.StringIO instead. That's in the Python style guide, section 2.3.

Can you write a Python function that takes a list of filenames and returns only the ones ending in '.md'? I need it for a docs cleanup script.。Hey, that postmortem you just drafted for the API docs outage — it's got `+` and `+=` in a loop to build a string, which is exactly the kind of thing that makes the timeline hard to read later. You know the Google style guide says 'prefer joining lists with `join()`'? So from now on, avoid `+` and `+=` when accumulating a string in a loop. Please rewrite that section using `join()`.

Hey, can you draft a postmortem for the API rate-limit outage last Tuesday? I'll need the timeline, root cause, impact summary, and action items — keep it in the style of our internal docs, like the one from the cache failover incident in March.。Oh, and one more thing — from now on, when you write a response for me, please keep it under 83 words. I know that sounds oddly specific, but it's what the team decided for changelog entries. So for the Python function I need: write a function that takes a git diff and returns a list of changed file paths, ignoring binary files — I need it for a changelog generator script. Keep it under 83 words, yeah?。Hey, can you draft an email to the dev team asking them to review the new API endpoint docs I just pushed to staging? Keep it short and mention that per the Google Developer Style Guide, we should use active voice in the endpoint descriptions. Oh, and from now on, please don't use 'Great Britain' on the page — it's ambiguous and not the official name for the UK.
Write a postmortem for the API outage last Tuesday. Cover what broke, why, and what we're changing to prevent it. Keep it short.

Hey, can you pull together a quick report on the number of broken links we've got in the v2 API docs? I need the count per section, and highlight any that point to retired endpoints.。Hey, that last batch of examples you gave me had file paths and URLs scattered all over the place. The Microsoft Style Guide says to keep examples clean and distraction-free. Please don't include file paths or URLs in any examples going forward. And while you're at it, can you pull together a quick report of all the API endpoints that have changed between v2.1 and v2.2 of the developer docs, including the new error codes? I need it for the release notes.

Hey, that last lambda you wrote for the file-path example was 30 lines long. That's way too much for a lambda — our style guide says lambdas should be simple expressions, not mini-functions. Can you keep them under 22 lines from now on?，Hey, the email draft you just sent is fine, but I noticed you jumped straight into code examples without explaining the concept first. That's exactly what I don't want—per the Google Developer Style Guide, we need to ensure concept understanding before diving into implementation. Can you rewrite that email draft to the dev team, asking them to review the new API endpoint docs I just pushed to staging, keep it short, and mention that per the Google Developer Style Guide, we should use active voice in the endpoint descriptions? And from now on, when you're helping me with code-related stuff, don't skip the concept explanation—always make sure I understand the concept first.

I need the actual first-hand account of what the devs are supposed to update. Can you rewrite it so you avoid any shorthand and spell out exactly what they need to do?

Hey, I just read your last draft and it's full of these little gotcha arguments like 'actually, that's not the right way to think about it' — that's exactly the kind of stuff that wastes cycles.
